Fact.Name: The IRC 1341 method is the deduction (computed lesser of the two methods)
Fact.Description: FALSE when the whole return's claim-of-right repayment does not exceed $3,000 (/claimOfRightRepaymentExceedsThreshold is false): there is no section 1341 method and no deduction for the repayment. Above $3,000, taxCalculations:/claimOfRightDeductionGivesLesserTax: TRUE when the tax computed with the Schedule A line 16 deduction is no more than the tax computed without it minus the earlier-year decrease (a tie takes the deduction), FALSE when the credit gives the lesser tax. Incomplete while that comparison is (for example while an earlier-year tax figure is unanswered), so neither the deduction (/claimOfRightRepaymentDeduction) nor the credit (schedule3:/sched3Line13b) is taken by default. Fact.Name: Other claim-of-right repayment included in an earlier year's income (writable)
Fact.Description: Question: "In 2025, did you repay any amount, other than unemployment compensation or social security benefits, that you included in your income in an earlier year because it appeared you had a right to it (for example, repaid wages)? If so, how much?" Help: "If you reported it as wages, unemployment compensation, or other nonbusiness income, you may be able to deduct it as an other itemized deduction if the amount repaid is over $3,000" (2025 Publication 525, Repayments, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p525.pdf, page 36). Count only amounts that were included in income in the earlier year; a repayment of an amount excluded from that year's income is not a claim-of-right repayment (IRC 1341(a)(1), 26 U.S.C. 1341, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section1341&num=0&edition=2024). Do not include a repayment of self-employment income or a capital gain: Publication 525 deducts those on Schedule C, Schedule F or Schedule D (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p525.pdf, page 36). Do not also enter this amount in /writableOtherItemizedDeductions. Asked on the claim-of-right repayment screen of every return, before the method election, whether or not the filer itemizes (the credit on Schedule 3 line 13b needs no itemizing); it feeds the $3,000 test, so it cannot be gated on it. Unanswered: $0 in /claimOfRightRepaymentTotal (read IsComplete first), the same as no repayment. Validation: Dollar, minimum $0. Feeds /claimOfRightRepaymentTotal, and through it the $3,000 threshold, the Schedule A line 16 deduction (/claimOfRightRepaymentDeduction) and the Schedule 3 line 13b credit (schedule3:/sched3Line13b).

Fact.Name: Total claim-of-right repayment on this return (the IRC 1341(a)(3) measurand)
Fact.Description: The whole return's claim-of-right repayment, the IRC 1341(a)(3) measurand: unemployment compensation included in an earlier year's gross income and repaid in 2025 (unemployment:/totalAmountPaidBackForBenefitsBeforeTaxYear), social security benefits in the same posture (socialSecurity:/socialSecurityRepaymentIncludedInEarlierYearIncome), and any other repayment of nonbusiness income included in an earlier year (/writableOtherClaimOfRightRepaymentIncludedInEarlierYearIncome). Summed before the $3,000 test because Publication 525 measures the total repaid on the return, not each repayment. The unemployment addend and the other-repayment writable are read IsComplete first: an unfinished 1099-G collection or an unanswered writable contributes $0, which can only fail to reach $3,000, never falsely clear it. The social security addend is Incomplete only when box 5 is below minus $3,000 and its earlier-year part is unanswered. Not rounded: the $3,000 test is a strict "exceeds", and rounding would move $3,000.01 to $3,000.00. Rounding happens once, at /otherItemizedDeductions. Not in this sum: repaid self-employment income or capital gains, which Publication 525 deducts on Schedule C, F or D rather than on line 16.

Fact.Name: The claim-of-right repayment exceeds $3,000 (IRC 1341(a)(3))
Fact.Description: STRICTLY greater than $3,000. The statute says "the amount of such deduction exceeds $3,000", and both publications say the same in the other direction — Pub. 915 denies the deduction when "the figure is $3,000 or" "less", Pub. 525 asks whether the amount repaid "was less than $3,000". So exactly $3,000.00 does NOT qualify and $3,000.01 does; the node-test pair claim-of-right-1341-boundary-3000-denies / claim-of-right-1341-boundary-3000-01-allows pins both sides. EXPORTED because this is the ONLY fact that can tell an intake surface the filer is ELIGIBLE for the section 1341 election. Its two neighbours /electsClaimOfRightRepaymentDeduction and /claimOfRightRepaymentDeduction both carried Export and this did not, which left the eligibility signal invisible outside this module — and the population the unit's own commit message is proudest of finding ($2,000 of unemployment plus $2,000 of social security, tripping neither module guard) is reached ONLY by someone asking the question. The dictionary cannot ask it; exporting the signal is the most this side can do, and the discovery step is SERVICE-side by invariant #7.

Fact.Name: Gifts to charity by cash or check (Schedule A line 11)
Fact.Description:
Schedule A line 11 as printed: EVERY cash or check gift, which this module splits into two AGI tiers for the limits. /allowableCharitableCash is the public charity tier and /charitable30PctOrgCashEntered is the complete safe view of the 30 percent organization tier, whose own fact states it is a line 11 sub component. The printed box is their sum, so neither fact alone may fill it. Both addends are the post Publication 570 apportionment amounts, which is what the publication says to enter on the line, and the AGI limits run downstream of this box rather than inside it.

LINE 5b IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS TEST, and the omission is load bearing. /writableRealEstateTaxesIncludedInStateLocalTaxes was authored as a PORTION intake - the real estate part OF the combined line 5d figure, collected only so the Publication 570 apportionment could reach it - so a return that answers the combined total plus that portion is the module's ORIGINAL supported shape and must keep resolving line 5d from the combined intake. Fact.Name: Average grandfathered mortgage debt (Pub 936 Table 1 line 1)
Fact.Description: Average eligible debt incurred on or before October 13, 1987, including only refinancings that retain grandfathered treatment under Pub 936. Classify and average debt under that publication, not by loan balance at year end. Enter zero when none. Answering either older-debt balance selects the detailed worksheet; both older balances, the post-2017 balance and filing status must then be complete. Do not exclude qualifying grandfathered interest merely because proceeds were not used for acquisition.

Fact.Name: Average pre-December-16-2017 acquisition debt (Pub 936 Table 1 line 2)
Fact.Description: Average eligible acquisition debt incurred after October 13, 1987 and before December 16, 2017. Include qualifying transition-rule or refinancing amounts in this category only after applying Pub 936. Exclude grandfathered debt, post-2017 debt and non-acquisition debt. Enter zero when none; partial older-debt answers do not fall back to the simplified calculation.

Fact.Name: Nonqualifying mortgage interest and points included in the entered total
Fact.Description: Interest and otherwise currently deductible points already included in the entered Schedule A lines 8a-8c or combined mortgage-interest total that are attributable to non-acquisition use of the debt, after applying tracing and the grandfathered-debt exception. This input is not a general adjustment for unamortized points, service fees, or other non-interest charges; remove those before entering eligible current-year interest and points. Exclude them before territory apportionment, debt limitation and the Form 8396 reduction. Do not enter principal or deduct the same exclusion twice. Zero explicitly confirms no exclusion from the entered amount. The amount cannot exceed the entered total. A true mixed-use checkbox requires this answer on a positive-interest return; a false checkbox conflicts with a positive exclusion. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540) Part II line 8 mortgage detection).

Fact.Name: Detailed mortgage debt breakdown was answered
Fact.Description: True when either older-debt amount is answered, including zero. This complete-safe presence predicate selects one authoritative calculation, never sums a legacy deduction and a detailed deduction.

Fact.Name: Detailed mortgage debt inputs are complete and nonnegative
Fact.Description: Checklist used only to enter the detailed calculation: all three average balances and the MFS predicate must be complete, with no negative balances. False is an input-completeness/consistency result, not a determination that a mortgage is ineligible.

Fact.Name: Pub 936 Table 1 line 3 old acquisition-debt limit
Fact.Description: One million dollars, or five hundred thousand for married filing separately. An unknown filing status leaves this detailed-path amount unresolved rather than selecting the larger cap.

Fact.Name: Pub 936 Table 1 line 6 qualified older debt
Fact.Description: The smaller of grandfathered plus pre-2018 acquisition debt and the larger of grandfathered debt or the old statutory limit. Grandfathered balances are not arbitrarily capped at one million dollars.

Fact.Name: Pub 936 Table 1 line 11 qualified loan limit
Fact.Description: The smaller of line 6 plus post-2017 debt and the larger of line 6 or the modern limit. This expression also implements the line-6 stop instruction: with no post-2017 debt, or with line 6 at or above the modern limit, the result is line 6. It does not stack an unrestricted one-million-dollar allowance on a separate seven-hundred-fifty-thousand-dollar allowance.

Fact.Name: Pub 936 Table 1 line 12 total eligible average mortgage debt
Fact.Description: Sum of the three eligible debt categories, not non-acquisition debt. Requires each category explicitly, so an unanswered category is not treated as zero.

Fact.Name: Validated nonqualifying mortgage amount
Fact.Description: Uses an answered nonnegative exclusion no larger than the source total. A positive exclusion with an explicitly false mixed-use answer remains unresolved. An unanswered exclusion is zero only on an entered-zero-interest return or in the legacy path where mixed use is not explicitly claimed. A true mixed-use claim with positive interest and no amount stays unresolved.

Fact.Name: Mortgage interest and eligible points after tracing
Fact.Description: Entered mortgage interest and currently deductible points less the validated nonqualifying portion. Uses the authoritative combined-or-components total exactly once. This is an input to apportionment, not a second line-8 deduction. Points must already satisfy Pub 936 Part I; this module does not calculate amortization or assume every Form 1098 point is deductible.

Fact.Name: Debt-limit fraction rounded to thousandths
Fact.Description: The detailed calculation divides Table 1 line 11 by line 12 and rounds to three decimal places, stored as an integer from zero through one thousand. Positive interest with a detailed zero denominator is unresolved. Without either older-debt answer, the pre-existing post-2017-only fraction remains, including its zero-balance bypass. A partial detailed answer never selects that fallback.

Fact.Name: Current-year other-organization noncash excess for carryover
Fact.Description: The apportioned current-year 30-percent-organization noncash gift less its own allowed deduction, floored at zero. Covers both K-1 code D and noncash gifts for the use of an organization in the existing shared tier. Excludes QCC excess, which has a different carryover period, and excludes prior-year carry-in. This character-specific output is added to the existing current-year excess aggregate; no future-year consumption or vintage allocation is invented.
